questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle of mass $m_1$ and electric charge $q$ starts from rest under the influence of a uniform external electric field $\mathbf{E}$ to travel a distance $d$ in time $t_1$. If the particle had mass $m_2$, it would take time $t_2$ to travel the same distance. What is the ratio $\dfrac{t_1}{t_2}$?
questions.solution:
Force on the particle is $F = qE$

Acceleration of the particle is $a = \dfrac{F}{m} = \dfrac{qE}{m}$

Using the equation of motion $s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u = 0$ and $s = d$:

$d = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{qE}{m} \right) t^2$

$t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2dm}{qE}}$

Since $d$, $q$, and $E$ are constant, $t \propto \sqrt{m}$

$\dfrac{t_1}{t_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m_1}{m_2}}$

Answer : $\sqrt{\dfrac{m_1}{m_2}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Three infinite plane sheets which have uniform positive surface charge densities $\sigma$, $\sigma$ and $2\sigma$, are arranged parallel to each other with a separation of $d$ as shown in the figure. A spherical Gaussian surface $S$ of radius $d/2$ has its center on the middle sheet. Which of the following statements regarding the electric flux $\Phi_L$ through the left hemisphere and the electric flux $\Phi_R$ through the right hemisphere of the Gaussian surface is correct?
questions.solution:
Let the middle sheet be located at $x = 0$. Then the left sheet is at $x = -d$ and the right sheet is at $x = d$.

The electric field in the region between the left and middle sheets ($-d \lt x \lt 0$), where the left hemisphere lies, is the superposition of the fields from all three sheets. Taking the rightward direction as positive:

$E_L = E_{\text{left}} + E_{\text{middle}} + E_{\text{right}}$

$E_L = \dfrac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0} - \dfrac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0} - \dfrac{2\sigma}{2\epsilon_0} = -\dfrac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0}$

The electric field $E_L$ is non-zero and points towards the left. Since the outward normal of the left hemisphere also points leftwards, the electric flux through the left hemisphere is positive ($\Phi_L \gt 0$).

The electric field in the region between the middle and right sheets ($0 \lt x \lt d$), where the right hemisphere lies, is:

$E_R = E_{\text{left}} + E_{\text{middle}} + E_{\text{right}}$

$E_R = \dfrac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0} + \dfrac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0} - \dfrac{2\sigma}{2\epsilon_0} = 0$

Since the electric field is zero everywhere on the right hemisphere, the electric flux through the right hemisphere is zero ($\Phi_R = 0$).

Comparing the two fluxes, we get $\Phi_L \gt \Phi_R$.

Answer: $\Phi_L \gt \Phi_R$.
